In mathematics, a '''uniformly disconnected space''' is a [[metric space]] <math>(X,d)</math> for which there exists <math>\lambda > 0</math>
such that no pair of distinct points <math>x,y \in X</math> can be connected by a <math>\lambda</math>-chain.
A <math>\lambda</math>-chain between <math>x</math> and <math>y</math> is a sequence of points
<math>x= x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_n = y</math> in <math>X</math> such that <math>d(x_i,x_{i+1}) \leq \lambda d(x,y), \forall i \in \{0,\ldots,n\}</math>.<ref>{{cite book| last = Heinonen| first = Juha | title = Lectures on Analysis on Metric Spaces | series = Universitext | publisher = Springer-Verlag | location = New York | year = 2001 | pages = x+140 | isbn = 0-387-95104-0}}</ref>

==Properties==

Uniform disconnectedness is invariant under [[quasi-Möbius map|quasi-Möbius maps]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Heer|first=Loreno|date=2017-08-28|title=Some Invariant Properties of Quasi-Möbius Maps|url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/agms-2017-0004/html|journal=Analysis and Geometry in Metric Spaces|language=en|volume=5|issue=1|pages=69–77|doi=10.1515/agms-2017-0004|issn=2299-3274|arxiv=1603.07521}}</ref>
